==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tḱey-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|posicioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|posicion}}, from {{der|en|la|positiō||a putting, position}}, from {{m|la|positus||placed, situated}}, past participle of {{m|la|pōnō||to place}}; see {{m|en|ponent}}. Compare {{m|en|apposition}}, {{m|en|composition}}, {{m|en|deposition}}; see {{m|en|pose}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/pəˈzɪʃ.ən/|[pəˈzɪʃ.n̩]|a=RP,GA,AuE}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-position.ogg|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-position.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/pəˈzəʃ.ən/|[pəˈzəʃ.n̩]|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪʃən|s=3}}
* {{hyph|en|caption=Hyphenation (UK)|po|si|tion||pos|i|tion}}, {{hyph|en|caption=(US, Indic)|po|si|tion}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[place]] or [[location]].
#: {{syn|en|stead<q:obsolete>}}
# A [[post]] of employment; a [[job]].
# A [[status]] or [[rank]].
#: {{ux|en|Chief of Staff is the second-highest '''position''' in the army.}}
# An [[opinion]], [[stand]]{{,}} or [[stance]].
#: {{ux|en|My '''position''' on this issue is unchanged.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1643|author=w:John Milton|title=Doctrine and Discipline of Divorce
|passage=The cause therfore of divorce expres’t in the '''position''' cannot but agree with that describ’d in the best and equalest sense of Moses Law.}}
# A [[posture]].
#: {{ux|en|Stand in this '''position''', with your arms at your side.}}
# {{senseid|en|situation}} {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[situation]] suitable to perform some action.
#: {{ux|en|The school is not in a '''position''' to provide day-care after 4:00 pm.}}
# {{lb|en|team sports}} A place on the [[playing field]], together with a set of duties, assigned to a [[player]].
#: {{ux|en|Stop running all over the field and play your '''position'''!}}
# {{lb|en|finance}} An amount of securities, commodities, or other [[financial instrument]]s held by a person, firm{{,}} or institution.
#: {{coi|en|[[long position|long '''position''']]}}
#: {{coi|en|[[naked position|naked '''position''']]}}
# {{lb|en|finance}} A [[commitment]], or a group of commitments, such as [[option]]s or [[future]]s, to buy or sell a given amount of [[financial instrument]]s, such as securities, currencies or commodities, for a given price.
# {{lb|en|arithmetic}} A method of solving a problem by one or two [[supposition]]s; also called the ''rule of trial and error''. <!--W1913-->
# {{lb|en|chess}} The full state of a [[chess]] game at any given turn.
# {{lb|en|poker}} The order in which players are seated around the table.
# {{lb|en|electronics}} A [[pin]]; a [[connector]].
